section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1982
title: Bengal (9 · 0 %), Kerala (7 · 6 %), Tamil Nadu (7 · 0 %), Bihar (6 · 6 %), Haryana (4 · 9 %), Gujarat (3 · 7 %), Tripura (3 · 6 %), J&K (1 · 7 %), Nagaland (1 · 2 %), Orissa (0 · 5 %), and Punjab (0 · 2 %). Rest of the States registered a decline in the total number of accidental deaths in 1982 over 1981. Union Territories The incidence of accidental deaths went up to 11 · 1 per cent in 1982 over 1981 in the Union Territories as a whole. The U.Ts. which registered a decline in the total number of accidental deaths in 1982 over 1981 were Mizoram (27 · 3 %), Goa, Daman & Diu (16 · 5 %), Arunachal Pradesh (14 · 1 %), while D&N Haveli did not register any change and Lakshadweep recorded only 3 cases of accidental deaths against nil in 1981. Rest of the U.Ts. registered an increase in total number of accidental deaths over 1981. Metropolitan Cities The incidence of accidental deaths recorded a decline of 14 · 0 per cent in 1982 over 1981 in the 12 metropolitan cities as a whole out of which 6 registered an increase and 6 registered a decline in the total number of accidental deaths during 1982 over 1981. notes: Male victims of accidental deaths accounted for 65.9 per cent of the total accidental deaths in the country during 1982 while the female victims were 34.1%. The ratio of male and female victims for the States as a whole was 65.6% and 34.4% respectively while for the Union Territories as a whole it was 73.6% and 26.4% respectively. This percentage of male and female victims for the Metropolitan Cities as a whole was 66.3% and 33.7% respectively.

The State of Nagaland recorded the highest percentage of male victims (89.9%), of the total accidental deaths recorded in the state followed by Jammu & Kashmir (84.9%), Meghalaya (84.4%) and Sikkim (81.7%). The remaining States recorded less than 80.0 per cent of male involvement of total accidental deaths.
The Union Territories viz., D&N Haveli, Mizoram and A&N Islands also recorded the highest percentage of male victims (93.7%), (89.3%) and (80.0%) respectively.
The detailed statistics may be seen in Table V.

The accidental deaths reported during 1982 have been further analysed according to age group of victims. On the all India level the highest number of accidental deaths occurred in the age group of 18-30 years which accounted for 36.1 per cent of the total accidental deaths followed by 30-50 years age group which accounted for 28.8 per cent of the total accidental deaths. While 21.5 per cent of the total accidental deaths occurred in the age group below 18 years, 13.6 per cent deaths were recorded in the age group of above 50 years. The distribution of accidental deaths according of age groups in the States as a whole did not very much from the all India figures and the distribution followed generally the same pattern in the Union Territories and the Metropolitan cities also.
